description: Jellyfin and Kavita. Both are .NET/Serilog, but they do NOT share an output template. Jellyfin: [2026-08-21 14:30:22.123 +02:00] [INF] [17] SourceContext: message. Kavita: [Kavita] [2026-08-22 00:00:08.413 +00:00  91] [Information] SourceContext message — an app-name prefix, the thread id inside the timestamp bracket rather than its own, a full-word level, and a space after the source context instead of a colon. Nothing in Jellyfin's patterns matches that, and with ignore_failure the line would keep its raw message and gain no timestamp, level or logger at all.

grok.description: The message body must be able to span newlines. Multiline joining happens in the agent, so by the time a stack trace reaches this pipeline it is one document whose message contains embedded newlines — but GREEDYDATA is `.*`, which does not cross them, and grok anchors `$` per line. The grok therefore *succeeded* on the first line alone and `set message copy_from _tmp.msg` then replaced the whole joined event with just that line, silently discarding every trace. MSGBODY is `(?s).*` so the body runs to the end of the document.

script.description: Normalise the level. Serilog's file sink writes three-letter abbreviations, but Kavita configures it for full words — INF and Information are the same level and must not become two different values of log.level, which is a case-sensitive keyword.
script.source: def m = ['VRB':'trace','VERBOSE':'trace','DBG':'debug','DEBUG':'debug','INF':'info','INFO':'info','INFORMATION':'info','WRN':'warn','WARN':'warn','WARNING':'warn','ERR':'error','ERROR':'error','FTL':'fatal','FATAL':'fatal','CRITICAL':'fatal']; def l = ctx._tmp?.lvl; if (l != null) { if (ctx.log == null) { ctx.log = [:]; } def k = l.toUpperCase(); ctx.log.level = m.containsKey(k) ? m[k] : l.toLowerCase(); }
